w:r.w:t: Design a detailed technical architecture for an internal "Knowledge Assistant" tool. This tool will allow internal teams to upload and analyze product-related documents (the "Knowledge Hub") to get specific answers with precise citations.
Support for PDF, Word (.docx), Excel (.xlsx), and Web Resources (URLs).
Users can manage up to 40 documents. The UI must allow users to "select" or "unselect" specific resources to narrow the scope of a particular query.
The AI must generate answers based
The direct quote from the source.
The location metadata/navigation (Page number for PDFs, Tab/Row for Excel, Section for Word/Web).
A custom web-based chat interface with a sidebar for document management.
Provide a general architecture that can be hosted on-premise or on a standard cloud provider.
Propose a model strategy that provides high reasoning quality while maintaining low operational costs (e.g., using smaller models for simpler tasks or efficient indexing).
A high-level diagram illustrating the data flow from ingestion to retrieval. This should include:
LLM orchestration layer (e.g., LangChain or LlamaIndex).
The candidate must address the following sections:
How will you handle Excel and Web resources specifically to ensure the AI understands the context?
Explain the chunking strategy and how you will map chunks back to physical locations (page/row) for citations.
How will the "Select/Unselect" feature be implemented at the database level to ensure low latency?
What database and storage solutions do you recommend for high-speed retrieval?
Describe how you would handle user authentication and session management for an internal tool.
Which LLM(s) do you recommend and why?
Describe the prompt engineering or "System Instruction" strategy to enforce strict citation formatting.
How will the system handle cases where the answer is
How does your design minimize "Token Waste"?
Briefly explain how the system could scale if the number of documents grew from 40 to 4,000.
Detailed mapping of data ingestion, processing, and retrieval flows.
Solves for precise quote extraction and provides clear location mapping logic.
Provides basic source links or names only.
Strategies for structured data like Excel and web scraping.
Standard handling of PDFs and text files.
Fails to address non-PDF file types.
Clearly explains how state management handles selected/unselected files.
Proposes a tiered approach (e.g., smaller models for simple tasks).
Uses a single high-cost model for everything.
A functioning prototype or code implementation of the core RAG logic.
A brief demo or a code snippet of the citation parsing logic will be highly regarded.
